DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http.•//w•MW.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 87 s. 2021 July 22, 2021 ATTY. VIC RUSKIN M. ONG Vice-Mayor Municipality of Gloria Oriental Mindoro Dear Vice-Mayor Ong: This has reference to your letter dated 17 May 2021 requesting for this Department's opinion on the authority of the Sangguniang Bayan ("SB") to grant legislative franchise for the establishment and operation of cockpit. Your query was forwarded to the Central Office by DILG- MIMAROPA Director Wilhelm Suyko through a 3rd Indorsement dated 04 June 2021 Particularly, the queries from your letter are herein replicated in verbatim: 1. Is it possible for the SB to grant legislative franchise despite the existence of the residential areas in the area? The applicant is arguing that they cannot be blamed for the action of adjacent property owners who constructed residential houses and commercial establishments beside the cockpit compound. 2. Is the authority to grant franchise a ministerial or act of the SB? 3. Ifthe SB will grant franchise despite existence of residential houses and commercial establishments within 200 lineal meters, will the members of the SB be liable for violation of the law? 4. Can the Zoning Ordinance disregard the requirement of PD449 in Section 5, thereby permitting the construction of cockpits, within or near existing residential or commercial areas, hospitals, school buildings, churches or other public buildings? 5. Can the Municipal Engineer be held liable for the issuance of building permit for the construction of cockpit within the 200-meter linear vicinity of the residential and commercial areas?

6. Can the Municipal Mayor issue mayor's permit in the absence of legislative franchise for the operation of a cockpit? At the outset, as to the first query, we opine in the negative. The Department respectfully emphasizes that a legislative franchise is a privilege grant from the local government as provided under Section 131 (m) of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), to wit: "Franchise" is a right or privilege, affected with public interest which is conferred upon private persons or corporations, under such terms and conditions as the government and its political subdivisions mav impose in the interest of public welfare securi and safe Accordingly, since a franchise is a right or privilege affected with public interest, it is mandatory for the applicant or the grantee thereof to abide by the laws, rules and regulations enacted in relation thereto. "Whenever a business is affected with public interest it may be subject to regulation to protect the public against danger and injustice" (Acebedo Optical Company, Inc. v. CA; G.R. No. 100152, 31 March 2000). Correspondingly, taking into account that Sec. 7(a) of Municipal Ordinance No. 9 s. of 2019 issued by the Sangguniang Bayan states that no cockpits shall be constructed, established, maintained and/or operated within a radius of two hundred (200) linear meters from any existing residential or commercial areas, hospitals, school buildings, churches or other public buildings, the applicant, owners of Gloria Cockpit Arena, must comply with the site and construction requirement. Moreover, the applicant's argument is untenable for the reason that Presidential Decree No. 449 (PD 449), otherwise known as the "Cockfighting Law of 1974", lays down the guidelines regarding cockpits site and construction, viz.. Section 5. Cockpits and Cockfighting: In General: (c) Cockpits Site and Construction. Cockpits shall be constructed and operated within the appropriate areas as prescribed in Zoning Law or Ordinance. In the absence of such law or ordinance the local executives shall see to it that no cockpits are constructed within or near existing residential or commercial areas. hospitals. school buildings. churches or other public buildinqs. Owners. lessees. or operators of cockpits which are now in existence and do not conform to this

requirement are given three years from the date of effectivity of this Decree to comply herewith. Approval or issuance of building permits for the construction of cockpits shall be made by the city or provincial engineer in accordance with their respective building codes, ordinances or engineering laws and practices. As can be gleaned from the afore-quoted provision, at the time the new building was constructed, both Municipal Ordinance No. 9 s. of 2019 and PD 449, were already in force and effect, thus the applicant must comply with the site and construction requirements. As to the second query, the grant of a franchise is discretionary act of the Sangguniang Bayan. As previously discussed, a franchise is a right or privilege affected with public interest issued by the local government, upon its discretion, after determining the private entity to be qualified to utilize the same. As to the third and fifth queries, we opine in the affirmative. The Deparmtent would like to highlight that the Supreme Court made a pronouncement in the case of Tan vs. Perea (G.R. No. 149743, 18 February 2005) that, while the LGC, now governs as to the authority of the Sangguniang Bayan to authorize or license establishment, operation, and maintenance of cockpits, it is still subject to the limitations laid down in PD 449. The Court even said that "there is no dichotomy between affirming the power and subjecting it to limitations at the same time. ' In that regard, Section 5(c) of PD 449 is explicit in providing that local executives shall see to it that no cockpits are constructed within or near existing residential or commercial areas, hospitals, school buildings, churches or other public buildings. Hence, to grant a franchise would be an abdication by the local government unit to regulate the site and construction of cockpits. Consequently, as to the fourth query, we opine in the negative. As previously mentioned, cockpits shall be constructed and operated within the appropriate areas as prescribed in Zoning Law or Ordinance and the applicant must strictly comply thereto. As to the sixth query, we opine in the negative. The Department would like to stress that the LGC places upon the Sangguniang Bayan, and not upon the Mayor, the authority to issue license for the operation of cockfight: "SECTION 447. Powers, Duties, Functions and Compensation. — (a) The sangguniang bayan, as the legislative body of the

municipality, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the municipality and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the municipality as provided for under Section 22 of this Code, and shall: (3) Subject to the provisions of Book II of this Code, grant franchises. enact ordinances authorizinq the issuance of permits or licenses. or enact ordinances levying taxes, fees and charges upon such conditions and for such purposes intended to promote the general welfare of the inhabitants of the municipality, and pursuant to this legislative authority shall: (v) Any law to the contrary notwithstanding, authorize and license the establishment, operation, and maintenance of cockpits, and regulate cockfiqhting and commercial breeding of gamecocks: Provided, That existing rights should not be prejudiced; " (Emphasis Supplied) This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Thank you. Very truly, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Undersec etary for Local Government COPY FURNISHED. DIR. WILHELM M. SUYKO Regional Director, DILG IV-B (MIMAROPA) 822 Quezon Avenue, Brgy. Paligsahan, Quezon City LLLS/32/17
